comparison: QSVC Q8-R1 vs. Classical RBF-SVM d=8
statistical_justification: Under 60 matched speaker x N conditions, Macro-F1 (diff=-0.0036, p=0.3428), Emergency Recall (diff=-4.37%, p=0.0689), False-Emergency Rate (diff=-1.20%, p=0.9505), and IPER (diff=-3.44%, p=0.0582) show no statistically significant difference after Holm-Bonferroni correction.
scientific_implication: The fidelity quantum kernel (ZZFeatureMap) provides zero empirical benefit over a classical RBF kernel for few-shot emergency intent classification.

comparison: QSVC Q8-R1 vs. Classical Adapter d=8
statistical_justification: Classical Adapter d=8 achieves statistically significantly higher Emergency Recall (45.81% vs. 27.52%, diff=-18.29%, p=2.5e-05) and higher IPER (14.21% vs. 8.25%, diff=-5.97%, p=0.0030). QSVC achieves higher Macro-F1 (0.1051 vs. 0.0949, p=0.0067) and lower false alarms (28.12% vs. 49.82%, p=3e-06).
scientific_implication: For safety-critical communication where missed emergencies are unacceptable, classical parameterized adapters remain substantially superior to quantum support vector classifiers.

statistical_justification: End-to-end Macro-F1 is statistically indistinguishable between 4 qubits and 8 qubits (diff=-0.0057, p=0.2025). Stage-2 subtype balanced accuracy increases modestly (29.84% -> 32.53%, diff=+2.69%, p=0.45).
scientific_implication: Expanding the Hilbert space dimension from 2^4=16 to 2^8=256 does not improve end-to-end classification performance under few-shot data constraints.

statistical_justification: Increasing circuit depth from reps=1 to reps=2 produces a negligible Macro-F1 shift (diff=-0.0019, 0.1051 -> 0.1070) while doubling total runtime (70.22s -> 128.04s, 1.82x increase).
scientific_implication: Additional feature map depth provides zero meaningful representation advantage in the low-resource regime.

comparison: QSVC Q8-R1 vs. Classical RBF-SVM d=8
statistical_justification: Per test evaluation inference time: QSVC is ~773x slower (1.0816s vs. 0.0014s). Total 60-condition experiment wall time: QSVC is ~213x slower (70.22s vs. 0.33s).
scientific_implication: Statevector simulation imposes massive computational overhead with zero classification gain. Hardware deployment would incur additional circuit execution and shot-noise overheads.
